content:
Short answer

What is HBM4? HBM4 is the fourth major generation of high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM placed next to AI accelerators. The JEDEC standard, published in 2025, doubles the interface to 2,048 bits per stack (from 1,024 in HBM3E), enabling around 2 TB/s per stack at standard speeds and more at higher speeds, with stacks of up to 16 dies and up to 64 GB per stack. HBM4 also allows a customisable logic base die. It powers next-generation accelerators such as NVIDIA's Rubin and AMD's MI400 series. Because AI workloads are increasingly limited by memory rather than compute, HBM4 is one of the most important hardware upgrades of 2026.

Why AI needs ever-faster memory

AI accelerators can perform far more calculations per second than their memory can feed them. Generating text with a large language model requires reading the model's weights for every token, so speed is often limited by memory bandwidth, not compute. Large models and long contexts also need huge capacity for weights and the KV cache. This "memory wall" is why AI chips use HBM instead of ordinary graphics memory. For the basics, see What is HBM? and GDDR7 vs HBM.

How HBM works (quick recap)

  • Several DRAM dies are stacked vertically and connected by thousands of through-silicon vias (TSVs).
  • A base (logic) die at the bottom manages the stack and connects it to the processor.
  • Stacks sit beside the GPU on a silicon interposer, connected by a very wide, short interface, using advanced packaging such as CoWoS.
  • Wide and short means huge bandwidth at relatively low power per bit.

HBM generations compared

Values are approximate and vary by vendor and speed grade.

What's new in HBM4

1. Double-width interface

HBM4 doubles the number of data channels and the interface width to 2,048 bits. Bandwidth can roughly double even without faster signalling, which helps keep power per bit under control.

2. Higher capacity

With taller stacks (up to 16 dies) and denser dies, a single stack can reach up to 64 GB. An accelerator with eight stacks could therefore carry hundreds of gigabytes of memory, enough to hold very large models on fewer chips.

3. Custom base dies

In earlier generations the base die was made by the memory supplier on a DRAM process. With HBM4, base dies can be manufactured on advanced logic processes (for example at TSMC) and customised for a specific customer, adding features such as better power delivery or even some processing close to memory. This blurs the line between memory and compute.

4. Reliability and power features

HBM4 adds improvements for reliability and power management needed at these densities and speeds.

Who makes HBM4

HBM is far harder to make than ordinary DRAM: stacking, TSVs and testing reduce yields, and each gigabyte uses more wafer area. Strong AI demand has kept HBM supply tight and prices high, which also affects ordinary memory markets. See why GPU prices are rising and the 2026 chip shortage.

Which AI chips use HBM4

  • NVIDIA Rubin: the successor to Blackwell, announced with 288 GB of HBM4 per GPU. See NVIDIA Rubin explained and the NVIDIA GPU roadmap.
  • AMD Instinct MI400 series: announced with up to 432 GB of HBM4.
  • Custom accelerators: hyperscalers' in-house AI chips are expected to adopt HBM4 in future generations.

Exact specifications and timing can change; check vendor announcements for current details.

What HBM4 means for AI workloads

Challenges

  • Cost: HBM is one of the most expensive parts of an AI accelerator.
  • Heat: taller stacks are harder to cool; HBM sits right next to a very hot GPU.
  • Packaging: larger interposers with more stacks push advanced packaging limits.
  • Supply: a few suppliers serve the whole AI industry, creating bottlenecks.

What comes after HBM4

The industry is already working on HBM4E with higher speeds, and longer-term ideas such as stacking memory directly on top of logic, optical connections between memory and compute, and processing-in-memory. The direction is clear: AI performance increasingly depends on moving data, not just computing on it.

Frequently asked questions

Is HBM4 faster than GDDR7?

Per chip, yes, by a wide margin. GDDR7 is cheaper and used in consumer GPUs like the RTX 5090; HBM4 is used in data center accelerators where bandwidth and capacity per chip matter most.

Will consumer graphics cards use HBM4?

Unlikely in the near term because of cost and packaging complexity. Consumer GPUs will continue using GDDR memory.

How much memory will HBM4 GPUs have?

Announced next-generation accelerators carry roughly 288 GB to 432 GB per GPU, depending on the design.

Why does memory matter so much for AI?

Because generating each token requires reading large amounts of data. Faster, larger memory directly increases speed and the size of models that fit. See GPU memory bandwidth.
